title: Why You Should Invest More In Your Health: round 1
sub: Long-form content, 16:9, re-edited from scratch from the 8/3 kitchen roll (C1511, 68:51 raw). The old edit was not used. The cut runs {TOTAL} and is not rendered yet: this round locks the look, the sound, the opening, the graphics and the clips first.
locked: Soft Blue Light graphics and the approved lower third template, text landing on your words; hard cuts, no swipe sounds, no camera movement; the shared voice chain; no burned captions and no AbsByAI.com mark at the end.

decisions.rec: D, bright and natural (used in the first minute)
opts: D: bright and natural (recommended, as built)
F: one step richer and darker
E: as bright as D with more contrast and colour
decisions.why: This kitchen set has never been through the new process, so there was no approved look to reuse. The camera original is dim and milky (the blacks are grey). I built four grades and looked at them full size beside your approved Work Out Every Day frames (the look you picked on 10-10) and the approved Belly Fat Emergency film. D lands closest to what you picked last time: your face is bright, your skin keeps the camera's own tone, the tank top is black and the fridge is clean. A looked dim on your face next to the approved frames. E made your arms go orange. F is the runner-up.

decisions.rec: 4, warm with less room echo (used in the first minute)
opts: 4: warm, less room echo (recommended, as built)
3: warm, room left as recorded
1: the lav as recorded
decisions.why: This room is more echoey than the Work Out Every Day kitchen (measured 87 against 69; your reference voice is 40). I built five treatments of the same 31 seconds and ran seven blind listening trials. The automatic default never won one and scored lowest, so it is out. The two warm versions won five of seven between them, and the listener could not reliably tell 3 from 4. I went with 4 because it is the voice you picked by ear on 10-10 and it brings the room from 87 down to 52. Both are below so you can hear them.

O2: the treadmill and the rising chart
Open on camera, no clip
decisions.why: Your first line is 'let's talk about why you need to be investing more in your health no matter how little you have right now'. There is no literal picture for that, so I went for a gag that acts it out, like the boxing glove you liked. Two concepts are below as start and end frames. The first minute shows O1 as a labelled placeholder.

opts: Approve all four (recommended)
Approve some: name them and say what to change
No new AI clips besides the opener
decisions.why: You do the excuse voice about 22 times in this film and the $5 clip budget covers four more clips after the opener, so I picked the four where a picture adds the most. A1 (0:20) the fat guy who has money, with his lips synced to your recording. A2 (15:11) the brokie turning out his pockets, surrounded by where the money went. A3 (23:51) the cardboard box house with a home gym beside it. A4 (46:25) the lawyer ironing his own shirt at his desk. A2 to A4 do not speak: your voice does the line. Frames are below; motion is only made after you approve them. Planned spend for all five clips: about $4.05.

opts: One film, 53 minutes, with the 31 chapters below (recommended)

decisions.why: Every retake, false start, crew aside and plain repeat is out (68:51 down to 53:04). What is left is your full argument, and I did not cut content for length. The chapter list is further down.

opts: Yes: build a full-screen phone card with meal photo calorie tracking at 19:29 and the workout and nutrition screens in the close (recommended, shown to you next round)
No: lower thirds only, as built
decisions.why: At 19:29 you say 'we can take a picture of it with our phone, track the calories', and the close lists the AI trainer and nutritionist. The approved app tour from the home workout video sits beside you, and this set has no room beside you (you fill the frame), so it needs a full-screen phone card like the one already used for the picture of yourself with abs. As built, those moments are you on camera with lower thirds.

opts: As built for now (recommended, nothing needed from you)
I will send phone photos or clips: say which
decisions.why: When you name your own things there is no footage of them, so you stay on camera with a lower third: your Purple mattress, your Oura ring and its sleep score, your Whoop or Apple Watch band, your shed gym (outside and inside), a Clean Eats delivery, a red light panel. Phone photos or a few seconds of phone video of any of these would go straight in.

ai.name: Opener, recommended: the health vending machine
ai.act: An office vending machine stocked with kettlebells, dumbbells, salmon and broccoli instead of snacks. An ordinary guy feeds in a crumpled dollar, a kettlebell drops out and he holds it up like a prize. Plays under your first line (0:00).

ai.name: Opener, alternative: the treadmill and the chart
ai.act: A tired man walks on a treadmill in front of a wall-size stock chart with a flat green line. As he picks up speed the line climbs to the top corner and he pumps his fist. Would play under the same first line.

ai.name: The fat guy who has money (your excuse voice, lips synced)
ai.act: A smug overweight businessman behind a desk stacked with cash says your line to camera, then shrugs. Plays under 'Making money is my first priority in life... I'll just be a fat guy who has money and I'll be happy with that' (0:20).
ai.cost: $0.80 for the take plus about $0.65 for the lip sync

ai.name: The brokie (15:11)
ai.act: A guy on his sofa turns his empty pockets inside out and shrugs, surrounded by pizza boxes, a bar cart, a tower of sneaker boxes and a giant TV. Plays under 'But I am a brokie, I don't have any money, so I just can't spend any money on my fitness, nothing I can do.' He does not speak.

ai.name: The cardboard box house (23:51)
ai.act: A cheerful guy crawls out of a cardboard box house with a full home workout setup laid out beside it, and starts swinging the kettlebell. Plays under 'Let's say you're literally homeless. You're living in the cardboard box.' Your real home setup follows it.

ai.name: The lawyer who has no time (46:25)
ai.act: A lawyer irons his own shirt on his desk with the phone clamped to his ear, a laundry basket on the client chair, then checks his watch. Plays under 'oh I got such a busy schedule, I'm a lawyer Dan, I don't have time to work out.' He is on the phone, so no lip sync is needed.

decided: Takes: where you said a line more than once I kept your last take when it was clean. Three places use an earlier take: 4:33 'top 10% of looks' (the retake says 'top 80%', a slip, right after 'the bottom 80% are getting nothing'); 39:36 'Here's the final thing you need to be investing in'; 45:03 the Clean Eats line (the last take drops 'every other week').

0:33: your last take of 'if money is your most important priority in life' has a small stumble on 'priority'. Takes 1 and 2 are clean but end 'then you must look good'. I kept the last take for its wording, 'then you need to be prioritizing your looks'.

Removed as plain repeats of the sentence before or after them: 'Okay so let's talk about the halo effect' (the third naming in 12 seconds), the second 'money does you no good if you're dead' at 12:05, the short inheritance-fights sentence at 12:34 (the next sentence tells the whole story), 'So go and buy yourself some vitamin D' at 41:21.

Stealing, 24:00 to 24:57: kept 'I would beg, I would borrow, I would steal' and your own retake 'I'm not endorsing stealing, but...'. The first, blunter take ('steal this stuff from the store') is out because you redid it.
Removed things said to the crew: silencing notifications, the junk food aside with the cameraman, the focus check, 'do a couple more takes of that'.

Kept out, as in your notes on the old edit: 'There's all kinds of problems...' at 6:28, the off-centre walk-in at 14:03, 'Your three options are...', and 'if you're middle class' at 39:36. Two hidden false starts the old edit missed are also out.
Closing call to action: one complete take.
Swearing and your opinions are untouched.

Hair: the camera framed the top of your hair right at the edge of the picture for most of this roll (it is clipped by a few pixels in about 7 frames of 10). Both sizes keep every row the camera recorded, and nothing is cropped further. There is no other take, so this cannot be fixed in the edit. One for Jeff on the next shoot.

No side list cards: you stand in the middle of a waist-up frame with no empty wall, so a card would sit on your arm. Lists come up as lower thirds, one part per item as you say it.
Music: none in this first minute. The quiet bed you chose for the last two videos goes in with the full film unless you say otherwise.
